records.impact_narrative_revenue:
This legislation recognizes $3.1 billion in greater than projected City funds revenues in Fiscal 2026. This is primarily driven by increases of $1.6 billion from the personal income and pass-through entity taxes and $310 million from the general sales tax. This was partially offset by a $335 million decrease in the business corporation tax. 
 
In addition, miscellaneous revenues increased by $56 million since the last revenue modification, including $30 million in fines and forfeitures and $47 million in miscellaneous revenue. This was partially offset by a $22 million decline in rental income. Unrestricted aid increased by $500 million.

program_breakdowns.program: Mental Health Services Pilot Program - Social Workers
program_breakdowns.description: Hiring of two social workers to administer mental health services to reunified children for the three-year pilot program.
program_breakdowns.offset_notes: Total includes prorated costs: $159,688 (FY27), $217,485 (FY28), $217,485 (FY29), $57,797 (FY30)

records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is anticipated that there would be no impact on revenues as a result of this legislation.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: The Council estimates that total cost of the enactment of this legislation would be $652,455 to hire two social workers to fulfill this legislation's requirements for the three-year period of the pilot. The annual salary for each social worker is estimated to be $72,495 with a 50 percent fringe rate for a total cost of $108,743 per year for each position. Because this legislation is anticipated to be effective for only a portion of Fiscal 2027, the prorated costs in that year are estimated to be $159,688. For Fiscals 2028 and 2029, the cost is estimated to be $217,485 per year. In Fiscal 2030 the cost is estimated to be $57,797, which is prorated for the portion of the year the program would be effective before it is deemed repealed. The Council estimates the pilot program would operate with 50 slots for eligible families and the two social workers to administer services. Based on the Council's analysis of current ACS operations and understanding of the removal process, youth who have been removed from their families and then reunified are typically already participating in court-mandated or other ACS-provided mental health services as part of the reunification process and the demand for this program is likely to only require the hiring of two additional social workers for the duration of the pilot.
records.omb_estimate_notes: The Office of Management and Budget did not provide an estimate.

records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is anticipated that there would be no impact on revenues as a result of this legislation.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: The Council estimates that total cost of the enactment of this legislation would be $652,455 to hire two social workers to fulfill this legislation's requirements for the three-year period of the pilot. The annual salary for each social worker is estimated to be $72,495 with a 50 percent fringe rate for a total cost of $108,743 per year for each position. The Council estimates the pilot program would operate with 50 slots for eligible families and the two social workers to administer services. Based on the Council's analysis of current ACS operations and understanding of the removal process, youth who have been removed from their families and then reunified are typically already participating in court-mandated or other ACS-provided mental health services as part of the reunification process and the demand for this program is likely to only require the hiring of two additional social workers for the duration of the pilot.

records.impact_narrative_revenue: It is anticipated that there would be no impact on revenues as a result of this legislation.
records.impact_narrative_expenditure: The Council estimates that total cost of the enactment of this legislation would be $652,455 to hire two social workers to fulfill this legislation's requirements for the three-year period of the pilot. The annual salary for each social worker is estimated to be $72,495 with a 50 percent fringe rate for a total cost of $108,743 per year for each position. Because this legislation is anticipated to be effective for only a portion of Fiscal 2027, the prorated costs in that year are estimated to be $159,688. For Fiscals 2028 and 2029, the cost is estimated to be $217,485 per year. In Fiscal 2030 the cost is estimated to be $57,797, which is prorated for the portion of the year the program would be effective before it is deemed repealed. The Council estimates the pilot program would operate with 50 slots for eligible families and the two social workers to administer services. Based on the Council's analysis of current ACS operations and understanding of the removal process, youth who have been removed from their families and then reunified are typically already participating in court-mandated or other ACS-provided mental health services as part of the reunification process and the demand for this program is likely to only require the hiring of two additional social workers for the duration of the pilot.

records.impact_narrative_expenditure: It is estimated that there would be no impact on expenditures resulting from the enactment of this legislation, as the agencies involved would be able to utilize existing resources to fulfill its requirements.
records.omb_estimate_notes: OMB did not provide an estimate.
